items.prompt: Black to move. White has built a pawn centre. Which move challenges it?

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is ...c5 (depth 16).
After ...c5 the pawn attacks the pawn on d4.
...e5 is rated at least half a pawn below the best move (depth 16).
At depth 16, 9...b4 is at least 0.1 pawns below ...c5.

hints: Which white pawn is the base of White's centre, and which black pawn can hit it?
A pawn break attacks the opponent's pawn chain from the side. Look at the c-file.
The c-pawn can step forward and attack d4.
items.explain: The c-pawn steps forward and attacks the pawn on d4, which stands next to the pawn on e4 in White's centre. A pawn that attacks a pawn from the side is a break. At depth 16 the engine puts ...c5 first; ...b4 is a different idea (it attacks the knight on c3) and is rated lower, and pushing the e-pawn instead is rated at least half a pawn lower.

feedback_by_move.e6e5: The e-pawn push gives White's pawn a capture and loosens d5. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least half a pawn below ...c5.
feedback_by_move.b5b4: The b-pawn attacks the knight on c3 but does not challenge the centre. The engine at depth 16 rates it lower than ...c5, so it is not the answer here.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is exf6 (depth 16).
White's pawn on e5 attacks the knight on f6.
Castling is rated at least three pawns below exf6 (depth 16).
a4 is rated at least three pawns below exf6 (depth 16).

hints: Which of White's pieces and pawns is attacked, and which black piece is attacked by a pawn?
A pawn that is attacked can sometimes capture instead of moving away.
The e-pawn takes the knight on f6.
items.explain: The pawn on e5 attacks the knight on f6, so it can capture instead of running. Other moves leave the knight on f6 alive; the engine at depth 16 rates castling and a4 at least three pawns lower. In this line the capture is close to forced.

feedback_by_move.e1g1: Castling ignores the knight. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least three pawns below exf6.
feedback_by_move.a2a4: a4 does not deal with the tension in the centre. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least three pawns below exf6.

items.prompt: White to move, move 11. This is the same position as the last one, except that Black's knight stands on g8 instead of f6. Does 11.Nxb5 work? Answer yes or no.

claims.statement: There is nothing on f6 for the pawn on e5 to capture.
At depth 16, 11.Nxb5 is at least a pawn below the best move.
At depth 16 White is not worse here: between -0.5 and +1.5 pawns.

hints: What did the pawn on e5 capture in the last position?
If the knight on c3 is traded for a pawn, what can White take back?
With nothing on f6, White has given a knight for a pawn.
items.explain: With the knight on g8 the pawn on e5 attacks only empty squares, so after 11.Nxb5 axb5 White has simply given a knight for a pawn. A forcing move needs a target. At depth 16 the engine rates 11.Nxb5 at least a pawn below its best move, and White is fine without it.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is ...Qb6 (depth 16).
The pawns on b5 and d4 are loose.
After ...Qb6 Black has no loose piece.
...e5 is rated at least 0.3 pawns below ...Qb6 (depth 16).
...Rg8 is rated at least 0.3 pawns below ...Qb6 (depth 16).

hints: Count the black pawns that are attacked. Are they defended?
One piece can stand where it protects both pawns.
The queen goes to b6.
items.explain: The pawns on b5 and d4 were both attacked and neither was defended. The queen on b6 defends both. The active rook move leaves a pawn loose; the engine at depth 16 rates it at least 0.3 pawns lower.

feedback_by_move.h8g8: The rook takes the open file but leaves the pawns loose. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least 0.3 pawns below ...Qb6.
feedback_by_move.e6e5: The pawn push opens lines for White's pieces without guarding b5 or d4. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least 0.3 pawns below ...Qb6.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is ...Rg4 (depth 16).
White attacks the pawn on d4 twice.
Black defends the pawn on d4 once.
After ...Rg4 Black defends d4 twice.
Castling queenside is rated at least 0.8 pawns below ...Rg4 (depth 16).

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders of d4.
A rook can defend a pawn along a rank if the squares between are empty.
The rook on g8 can step to g4 and look along the fourth rank.
items.explain: White attacks d4 twice (the knight and a rook) and Black defends it once. The rook goes to g4 and defends the pawn along the fourth rank, so the count is two against two. Castling queenside is natural, but the engine at depth 16 rates it at least 0.8 pawns lower.

feedback_by_move.e8c8: Castling queenside looks safe and develops the rook, but d4 stays defended once. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least 0.8 pawns below ...Rg4.
feedback_by_move.b7f3: Taking the knight removes one attacker but gives up a bishop. The engine at depth 16 rates it far below ...Rg4.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is Nxe6 (depth 16).
After Nxe6 the rook and the bishop both attack the knight on d7.
After Nxe6 only the king defends d7.
a4 is rated lower than Nxe6 (depth 16).
h3 is rated at least a pawn below Nxe6 (depth 16).

hints: Which black piece is hard to defend, and which white pieces point at its square if a line opens?
The knight on d4 stands between the rook on d1 and the knight on d7. Moving it opens the file.
The knight can capture on e6.
items.explain: The knight on d4 blocks the d-file. When it captures on e6, the rook on d1 and the bishop on b5 both attack the knight on d7, and only the king defends it. The engine at depth 16 rates Nxe6 first and a4 slightly lower; h3 is at least a pawn lower. A quiet move was close, so this is a choice of method, not a forced win.

feedback_by_move.a2a4: a4 takes space and is only slightly behind Nxe6 in the engine's depth-16 rating.
feedback_by_move.h2h3: h3 attacks the rook on g4 but gives Black time to organise. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least a pawn below Nxe6.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's knight on e6 attacks the bishop on f4. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is ...fxe6 (depth 16).
...Bxg3 is rated at least 1.5 pawns below ...fxe6 (depth 16).
...Be5 is rated at least 1.5 pawns below ...fxe6 (depth 16).

hints: What can capture the knight on e6?
Taking the knight is the simplest answer. Check what that capture opens.
The f-pawn takes on e6.
items.explain: The f-pawn takes the knight that came to e6. The engine at depth 16 rates the bishop moves at least 1.5 pawns lower: they leave the knight on a strong square. Taking is right, even though it opens the d-file.

feedback_by_move.f4g3: The bishop takes a pawn but leaves the knight on e6 and the knight on d7 under fire. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least 1.5 pawns below ...fxe6.
feedback_by_move.f4e5: The bishop move leaves the knight on e6. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least 1.5 pawns below ...fxe6.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's rook has just taken the knight on d7. Can the black king capture it?

claims.statement: Kxd7 is not legal.
The bishop on b5 attacks the square d7.
The engine's best move is ...Kf8 (depth 16).

hints: Which white pieces attack d7 besides the rook?
A king cannot capture onto an attacked square.
The bishop on b5 defends the rook on d7, so the capture is illegal.
items.explain: The rook on d7 is defended by the bishop on b5, so the king cannot take it: the capture would put the king on an attacked square. This is what made the sacrifice work: the rook landed on d7 and stayed. The engine at depth 16 gives ...Kf8 as Black's best.

items.prompt: White to move, move 29. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is Rd1 (depth 16).
Ra3 is rated at least 0.6 pawns below Rd1 (depth 16).
Qe3 is rated at least 2 pawns below Rd1 (depth 16).
The engine at depth 16 rates the position between -1.2 and +0.2 pawns, White's point of view.
The c-, d- and g-files are open.
After Rd1 White's rook stands on the open d-file.

hints: Look at the files: which one is open, and who could use it?
A rook has more work on an open file than on the a-file behind its own pawn.
The rook on a1 goes to d1.
items.explain: The game continued with Ra3. At depth 16 Rd1 is at least 0.6 pawns better and Qe3 at least two pawns worse. One visible difference: the d-file is open, and Rd1 puts the rook on it, while on a3 the rook is off the centre files [I]. Why the engine prefers Rd1 beyond that we cannot prove. Ra3 was a slip, not the end: the real collapse came four moves later with 33.Bd3.

feedback_by_move.a1a3: The game move. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least 0.6 pawns below Rd1.
feedback_by_move.e2e3: The queen offers a trade at once. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least two pawns below Rd1.

items.prompt: White to move, move 11. This is the game position: Black's knight stands on f6. Does 11.Nxb5 work? Answer yes or no.

claims.statement: 11.Nxb5 is legal.
At depth 16 the engine's first choice is 11.Nxb5.
After 11.Nxb5 axb5 White's pawn on e5 attacks the knight on f6.

hints: After 11.Nxb5 axb5, which black piece does the pawn on e5 attack?
The knight on f6 is attacked by a pawn that can capture it. What follows?
The pawn takes on f6 next, so the sacrifice has a target.
items.explain: After 11.Nxb5 axb5 the pawn on e5 attacks the knight on f6 and 12.exf6 follows, so the knight sacrifice has a target. At depth 16 the engine puts 11.Nxb5 first. Compare the same position with the knight on g8, where it does not work.
